newsitem.title: CANADA: Cominco buys zinc after smelter glitches.
newsitem.headline: Cominco buys zinc after smelter glitches.

text.p: Cominco Ltd said on Thursday that start-up problems with a new smelter at its Trail, British Columbia facility forced it to buy zinc on world markets in the second quarter.
That hurt the mining company's earnings for the quarter, which fell to C$0.20 a share from C$0.23 a year earlier, Cominco said.

During the start-up of the new Kivcet lead smelter, "operating disruptions have reduced production and necessitated the purchase of zinc from the London Metal Exchange to meet strong customer demand," Cominco said.
The Trail facility produces both zinc and lead and the two processes are integrated. A Cominco spokeswoman declined to say how much zinc the company bought.

Cominco said its zinc production at Trail for the quarter fell 11,400 tonnes from the year earlier to 59,100 and lead production at Trail fell 7,700 tonnes to 17,600. About three-quarters of the reduction was due to the Kivcet smelter start up, Cominco said.

Despite the problems with the smelter and slag fuming furnace, Cominco said the smelter start-up had progressed well and "the processes have demonstrated that they can meet the design objectives for processing zinc residues, the large accumulated stockpiles of which are carried at nominal cost in the financial statements."
Cominco said it expected problems to be resolved with the smelter and design production rates to be achieved by the end of the third quarter.
Teck Corp is a major shareholder in Cominco.
